title: Week 9 Warm-Ups
intro: Three short review questions each day: two free-response and one multiple-choice. Every question reviews content from earlier sections, not the section being taught that day.

instances.label: Original
instances.stem_html: A delivery robot moves west at 9 m/s. Three seconds later it is still moving west, but only at 3 m/s. Take east as positive. Find its average acceleration (include sign and units). Is the robot speeding up or slowing down? Explain.

instances.label: Original
instances.stem_html: A hockey puck glides straight across nearly frictionless ice at constant velocity after being struck. A classmate says, “Something must keep pushing it or it would stop.” Explain whether the puck needs a forward force to keep moving.

instances.label: Original
instances.stem_html: A cart is moving to the right. Its velocity changes from +2 m/s to +8 m/s over 3 s. Which statement best describes its motion?
choices: It moves right and speeds up with positive acceleration.
It moves left and speeds up with positive acceleration.
It moves right and slows down with negative acceleration.
It is not accelerating because it moves in one direction.
It moves left and slows down with zero acceleration.

instances.label: Original
instances.stem_html: A cyclist rides east at 11 m/s, then slows to 3 m/s east in 4 s. Take east as positive. Calculate average acceleration and explain why its sign makes sense.

instances.label: Original
instances.stem_html: Two toy cars each travel at a steady 6 m/s on straight tracks. One moves north and the other south. Compare their speeds and their velocities. What information must be included when reporting velocity?

instances.label: Original
instances.stem_html: A cart moves in a straight line at constant velocity while a 14 N force pulls right and friction acts left. What must be true about the friction force?
choices: Friction is 0 N because the cart moves.
Friction is 28 N left because it is moving.
Friction is 14 N left, giving zero net horizontal force.
Friction is 14 N right, helping the pull.
The friction cannot be compared without knowing the cart’s mass.

instances.label: Original
instances.stem_html: A steel ball is released from rest and falls for 2.0 s. Ignore air resistance and use g = 10 m/s². What is its speed after 2.0 s? Include its direction and explain the change in speed.

questions.topic: Acceleration and slowing while moving left

instances.label: Original
instances.stem_html: A skateboarder rolls left while slowing down. Choose right as positive. State the sign of the skateboarder’s velocity and the sign of its acceleration. Explain how you know.

instances.label: Original
instances.stem_html: A heavy metal ball and a lighter metal ball are released together from the same height in a vacuum. What should happen?
choices: The heavier ball falls faster because it weighs more.
The lighter ball falls faster because it has less mass.
Both balls accelerate downward at the same rate and land together.
Neither ball accelerates because there is no air.
The heavier ball has zero acceleration but a higher speed.

instances.label: Original
instances.stem_html: A pebble is dropped from a bridge. Ignoring air resistance, use g = 10 m/s² and d = ½gt² to find how far it falls in the first 2.0 s. Explain why it does not travel the same distance in every second.

instances.label: Original
instances.stem_html: In a Vernier ramp trial, a cart’s velocity down the ramp is 0.2 m/s at 0 s, 0.6 m/s at 0.5 s, and 1.0 m/s at 1.0 s. Find its average acceleration from 0 to 1.0 s. Would its velocity–time graph slope upward, downward, or stay flat?

instances.label: Original
instances.stem_html: Which situation best represents ideal free fall?
choices: A parachutist descending at constant speed with the parachute open.
A coin falling after release when air resistance is negligible.
A toy car rolling down a ramp.
A paper coffee filter drifting downward slowly through air.
A basketball resting on the gym floor.

instances.label: Original
instances.stem_html: Two marbles are dropped from rest in separate trials. One falls for 1.0 s and the other for 3.0 s. Using d = ½gt² with g = 10 m/s², calculate the distance each falls. How many times farther does the second marble fall?

instances.label: Original
instances.stem_html: A remote-controlled car travels west and speeds up from 4 m/s west to 10 m/s west in 3 s. Take east as positive. Find its average acceleration, including sign and units. Why can a negative acceleration mean speeding up here?

instances.label: Original
instances.stem_html: A ball tossed straight upward reaches its highest point. Ignoring air resistance, which statement is correct at that instant?
choices: Both velocity and acceleration are zero.
Velocity is upward and acceleration is zero.
Velocity is momentarily zero, but acceleration is downward.
Velocity is momentarily zero, and acceleration points upward.
Velocity is downward, and acceleration is upward.
